title_en: Germany pushed through Luxembourg and forced Slovakia to beat themselves
text_en: Germany pushed through Luxembourg and forced Slovakia to beat themselves Bobček helped his team secure a long-awaited win that guaranteed at least a play-off spot about 1 hour ago In a World Cup 2026 qualifier, the Germany national team won convincingly away at Luxembourg. The hero of the match was Woltemade, who scored a brace within twenty minutes of the second half, giving his side a comfortable position before the last round. Slovakia beat Northern Ireland at home thanks to a dramatic goal by Bobček already in stoppage time, in the 91st minute. In the second half the Slovaks twice started celebrating, but the goals of Škriniar and Strelec were disallowed by the referee: one for offside, the other for handball. At the end of the match the visitors were left with ten men after Ballard was sent off in the 99th minute. Germany have 12 points and lead Slovakia on goal difference before the last round. Northern Ireland (6) ended their fight for the 2026 World Cup. World Cup 2026. title_en: Joaquin Phoenix quit the film in which he was to play a gay character at the last minute
text_en: Joaquin Phoenix quit the film in which he was to play a gay character at the last minute Last week it emerged that Joaquin Phoenix suddenly withdrew from Todd Haynes's film about a gay love story, just five days before filming was to begin. The sudden withdrawal of the Oscar-winning star from the untitled film, set in the 1930s, has caused great anger in Hollywood. Legal action against Phoenix is expected. A source who spoke to Variety about Phoenix, who is known to have brought the project to director Todd Haynes, said the famous actor was afraid. The film was to focus on the intense love between the characters played by Phoenix and his other lead, Danny Ramirez. The project, whose financing depended on Phoenix's participation, has now effectively been shelved. A set had been built in Guadalajara, Mexico, where the shoot was to take place. Phoenix quit the project in early July, just a few days before the planned shoot, leaving the cast and crew in a difficult position. The film's producer Christine Vachon said what happened was completely unexpected and described the process as a nightmare. Various sources say that Joker star Phoenix was reluctant to play a gay character and to take part in some of the film's harsh scenes, while director Haynes said in an earlier interview that it was Phoenix who pushed the film to go further with more explicit scenes. Calls for legal action against Phoenix, who has caused anger among the producers, are growing. In Hollywood history there are examples of actors held responsible for leaving films without a star, paying compensation, or being forced to sign new film deals with the studio. When Bruce Willis left the Disney film Broadway Brawler midway through production, he had to make three Disney films below market rate as compensation. However, two of those films, Armageddon and The Sixth Sense, were very successful, and the situation turned in the actor's favor. It was also claimed that Phoenix almost quit Napoleon, the film he most recently appeared in and which attracted much attention, at the last moment. It was claimed that he threatened to leave the film directed by Ridley Scott unless Paul Thomas Anderson was brought in to rewrite it.

title_en: Sinner, the cat, the Panda: "We'll make you a statue", what's going on | Libero Quotidiano.it
text_en: Sinner, the cat, the Panda: "We'll make you a statue", what's going on | Libero Quotidiano.it Thanks to the katze. Meaning 'cat', in German. The cat of Jannik Sinner, an unusual protagonist of the weekend together with the little Panda of the world number 1 in tennis. Meaning this time the little Panda, the utility car par excellence. The Fox of San Candido is somewhat the Clark Kent of world sport. On court, on concrete but also on clay and maybe on the grass of Wimbledon, he is a Superman sometimes dressed in an equally questionable way. But off the court, in real life, he is a normal guy. Too normal. For some a 'loser'. A 'mountain man'. And so the teasing begins. Perhaps it's that German accent that makes him seem so unsophisticated. Perhaps it's because he prefers an extra training session on his serve to gossip, as confirmed by the fact that for months he was dating Anna Kalinskaya and there are barely a handful of photos of the two of them together. Or perhaps it's because he prefers to stay quiet, both when he isn't playing and, above all, when he is, rather than pumping his fists or touching his ear, winking at the crowd and putting on a bit of a show like his nemesis, Carlos Alcaraz. Now, remember the cat and the Panda? This story involves exactly the Spaniard who a week ago beat him at Roland Garros in one of the most epic Slam finals ever (certainly the longest). After the Parisian hangover, the phenomenon from Murcia thought it wise to 'switch off' by going to Ibiza, first to a nightclub and then to the beach. Friends, wild dancing, phone, a few cocktails. And everyone down to applaud him: well done, you're a winner, enjoy life, that's how it's done. His coach, Juan Carlos Ferrero, did in truth give him a bit of a scolding: «I told him to remember that he is always a tennis player. We already know the situation. He'll have fun and when he comes back he'll be in a good mood and recharged». Jannik instead, defeated and downcast, decided to recharge his batteries by going home, to his Dolomites. Not exactly the ugliest place on Planet Earth. Yet, perhaps also because of the defeat, choosing to spend a few days with mum Siglinde and dad Hanspeter has made him seem a 'sad sack'. A big baby of almost 24. And imagine when it became known that instead of partying, he is in the habit of doing something else. «He came back for a short time but this time I didn't manage to meet him. The last time we saw each other he was driving mum's Panda to take the cat to the vet», revealed the mayor of Sesto Pusteria, Thomas Summerer, to Un giorno da pecora on Rai Radio 1. Dagospia, as is its habit, piles on by talking of 'self-punishment'. But seeing and hearing him, after a win or a defeat, one tends rather to think that for Sinner, returning to the places and people he had to leave as a child because of an extraordinary talent is in fact a relief, a panacea for the very minor ills of his career. title_en: Risk for astronauts - 50 'problem areas' and four cracks on the ISS
text_en: Risk for astronauts - 50 'problem areas' and four cracks on the ISS The International Space Station ISS, which is to keep operating until the year 2030, is getting on in years. This brings age-related technical problems. A NASA report now warns of 50 'problem areas' and four cracks on the station, and a risk for the crew. For almost a quarter of a century, astronauts have been living without interruption aboard this outpost of humanity in space. With the station ageing, the US space agency NASA faces the challenge of ensuring crew safety on board and maintaining continuous operation. 'Major safety risk' for astronauts According to a recently published report by NASA's Office of the Inspector General (OIG), in connection with a leak in the Russian segment of the ISS, known since 2019, a 'major safety risk' for the astronauts on board has been identified. The NASA Office of Inspector General carries out reviews, investigations and audits of NASA programmes to prevent and uncover abuse, waste, fraud and mismanagement. The cracks had been covered by Roscosmos, the Russian counterpart of NASA, with a 'combination of sealant and patches', the US space agency said in a statement to the 'Washington Post'; repairs are under way. In the internal risk assessment, the leaking areas were rated 5 on a scale up to 5, the highest risk, according to the OIG report. Leaks near a hatch 'We have communicated the seriousness of the leaks several times, including when I was in Russia at the beginning of the year', deputy administrator Jim Free is quoted as saying in an interview with the 'Washington Post'. Because the leaks are near a hatch, Roscosmos complied with a NASA request to close the hatch as far as possible, Free said: 'We reached a compromise under which the hatch is closed in the evening.' Series of leaks in Russian modules In recent years, leaks in Russian hardware have repeatedly caused problems on the ISS. A dramatic incident occurred in December 2022, when a 'Soyuz' capsule began rapidly losing coolant (picture below) into space before a planned Russian spacewalk, which was then immediately cancelled. With hardly any other options, the Russian space agency Roscosmos sent an empty 'Soyuz' capsule to the ISS and brought the leaking spacecraft back to Earth empty for analysis. In February last year, an ammonia leak occurred on the Russian cargo spacecraft 'Progress 82' while it was docked at the space station. Seven months later another leak was discovered, this time in the Russian multipurpose laboratory module 'Nauka'. Space station to be operated until 2030 Construction of the ISS in orbit began in 1998. Japan, Canada, the USA and the participating countries of the European Space Agency (ESA) want to operate the space station until 2030. Russia, which is extremely important as a partner in space, has so far committed only to operation until 2028, but is open to continued operation until 2030.

title_en: Lyamkin on the clash in the match with Lokomotiv: 'Radulov understood who he was getting into, wanted to take Miller out of the game. We will never let a partner be offended'
text_en: Lyamkin on the clash in the match with Lokomotiv: 'Radulov understood who he was getting into, wanted to take Miller out of the game. We will never let a partner be offended' Lyamkin on the clash in the match with Lokomotiv: 'Radulov understood who he was getting into, wanted to take Miller out of the game. We will never let a partner be offended' Defenceman of Ak Bars Nikita Lyamkin, after the win over Lokomotiv (5:1, 1-1) in the final series of the Gagarin Cup, commented on the mass brawl at the end of the game. – You've been simply crushing your opponent in the first period two matches in a row. What's behind that? – I wouldn't say we're crushing them, we're just doing our job and understand how important it is to score first. – You don't have fights like the ones in the series with Avangard and Lokomotiv. What do you attribute that to? – There's still something to it, but we're here for hockey, we try to play. – You ran to defend Miller without a second thought. Was that a scratch from there? – Sanya [Radulov] slipped in a bit. I tried not to get involved in the fight, but we'll never let our partner be offended, especially since Sanya understood who he was getting into, wanted to take him out of the game, but we won't allow it, said Lyamkin.

title_en: Milos: Municipality prepares legally against exploratory drilling
text_en: Milos: The Municipality prepares legally against exploratory drilling Municipality of Milos moves from politics to legal action The Municipality of Milos has decided to legally fortify its position against the planned exploratory geothermal drilling, by assigning to a specialised law firm the evaluation of the Environmental Impact Assessment for the project Exploratory Geothermal Drilling on the Island of Milos. The decision follows the unanimous political stance of the Municipal Council against plans for geothermal activity on the island. According to the decision, the legal review is not limited to the technical analysis of the study, but will also examine the Municipality's options for intervention at administrative or judicial level, where the legal preconditions arise. - The project concerns exploratory drilling at the sites of Agrilies and Komia – Tsiglures. - The cause of concern is Milos's previous experience with geothermal activities and the existing extractive burden. - Milos combines intense tourist development and a distinctive geological character, elements that will be assessed in the legal opinion. The points to be examined include the legality of the siting, its compatibility with the existing land uses and with spatial and urban planning, as well as any restrictions due to special protection regimes. Particular attention will be paid to the completeness of the study and to whether it takes into account the cumulative pressures the island already faces from extractive activities. The opinion will record the Municipality's options for intervention and will look for points in the study that could be used at administrative or judicial level. In addition, the stages of the licensing procedure at which the Municipality may intervene and the available administrative tools will be analysed, as well as the relevant case law of the Council of State on projects with significant environmental impacts. This assessment is of strategic importance, given the multiple burdens the island has already faced. For the residents of Milos this move marks a shift from public protest to organised legal response, with the aim of exploring all the legal and administrative means the institutional framework offers. This development is critical for the protection of natural resources, the tourist economy and quality of life on the island.

title_en: Grave of former Chief Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation Savaş not visited on death anniversary
text_en: Grave of former Chief Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation Savaş not visited on death anniversary It drew attention that no one visited the grave of former Chief Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation Vural Savaş on the anniversary of his death. The grave of Vural Savaş, Chief Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation, who died at the age of 84 on 15 February 2023 in a hospital in Ankara where he was receiving treatment, was not visited on the anniversary of his death. Chief Prosecutor Savaş was elected a member of the Court of Cassation in 1987 and became Chief Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation in 1997. 'Requested a political ban for Erbakan' Months after the period known in Turkey's recent political history as 28 February, the Welfare Party was closed and its officials were given political bans. A five-year political ban was imposed on, primarily, Welfare Party Chairman Necmettin Erbakan, Şevket Kazan, Ahmet Tekdal, Şevki Yılmaz, Hasan Hüseyin Ceylan and İbrahim Halil Çelik. In the indictment prepared by the then Chief Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation Vural Savaş on grounds of acts contrary to the secular republic principle, policies in the Welfare Party programme such as ensuring spiritual development, establishing a Just Order, achieving heavy industry, increasing relations with Islamic countries and abolishing interest were seen as grounds for the closure case. On the second anniversary of his death, the grave of former Chief Prosecutor Savaş, located in the Gölbaşı Cemetery in Ankara, was not visited.

title_en: Amfissa: Bralos–Amfissa works in full swing, completion in February 2028
text_en: Amfissa: Bralos–Amfissa works in full swing, completion in February 2028 Progress and timetable for the Bralos–Amfissa section Construction works on the Bralos – Amfissa section of the Lamia – Itea – Antirrio road axis, one of the most demanding technical projects in the country, are in full swing. The official estimate states that the project is expected to be completed in February 2028. This 24-kilometre section is the most complex part of the diagonal axis and includes a series of major engineering structures that radically change access to Amfissa and Fokida. The contract between the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport and the company ABAX provides, among other things, for: - Construction of two tunnels with a total length of about 4.7 km. - Seven bridges with a total length of over 1 km. - Six junctions (at-grade and grade-separated) and underpasses. - A new network of secondary roads to be connected to the existing network. «Instead of one dual-carriageway tunnel, it was decided to build two independent single-direction tunnels, with the aim of enhancing road safety.» Technical features and local consequences The most important tunnel will be about 2,200 metres long and stands out as the dominant engineering work of the section. In parallel, the 2 km Gravia bypass and the 5 km Gravia – Bauxite Mines bypass are being implemented, raising the total length of the sections under construction to 31 km. For the local communities of Amfissa and Fokida, these works mean: - A significant reduction in travel times to Aetolia-Acarnania and Fthiotida. - Increased road safety, also thanks to the new tunnel design. - Better connection to major road networks and ports (Volos, Patras), which may boost local transport and the economy. The project is part of the European E65 road network and is funded by the Transport 2021–2027 programme. The operation of the axis as an expressway is expected to affect local flows of trade, tourism and travel, especially in peak seasons. Works and everyday life in Amfissa For Amfissa residents the works have immediate practical consequences: changes to usual routes, seasonal or permanent traffic arrangements on local roads, and an increased presence of heavy vehicles transporting materials. At the same time, with the completion of the axis, access to services and markets in other regions is expected to improve, which may facilitate business activity and tourist traffic. The local government and technical services should monitor traffic arrangements and safety measures during construction, so that any disruptions to residents' daily lives are kept to a minimum. In addition, making use of the new transport capacity after the works are handed over will require planning for tourism, commercial transport and the protection of the local environment. The handover of the Bralos–Amfissa section in 2028 will mark a turning point in linking eastern and western Greece, with tangible consequences for Amfissa and Fokida in terms of accessibility, safety and economic activity.

title_en: Gold exchange price exceeded $2450 per ounce for the first time since 20 May
text_en: Gold exchange price exceeded $2450 per ounce for the first time since 20 May The price of gold on Tuesday rose above $2450 per troy ounce at one point. The precious metal has been trading at these levels for the first time since 20 May, according to data from the Comex exchange. As of 17:02 Moscow time, the August gold futures contract cost $2448,85 per troy ounce (+0,82%). The daily high was 2452,55 per troy ounce. In May India removed more than 100 tonnes of its gold from the United Kingdom to place it in domestic vaults. This will allow New Delhi to save significantly on storing reserves abroad. At the end of March India's gold reserves were estimated at 822,1 tonnes. Meanwhile, Russia's gold reserves fell to $424 billion by the start of the second quarter. Moreover, according to experts' estimates, the total volume of gold in the private stashes of Russians exceeds the reserves of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation.

title_en: Claiming to be abandoned by KBRI Phnom Penh (Indonesian Embassy), problematic Indonesian citizens turn out to be repeat online fraud perpetrators
text_en: Claiming to be abandoned by KBRI Phnom Penh (Indonesian Embassy), problematic Indonesian citizens turn out to be repeat online fraud perpetrators jakarta.jpnn.com - Indonesian Ambassador to the Kingdom of Cambodia Santo Darmosumarto has spoken out about the claim of four Indonesian citizens from Binjai, North Sumatra, who said they had left an online fraud company. The four Indonesian citizens from Binjai asked for facilities from the KBRI so they could return to Indonesia. They said they received a monthly salary, their movements were not restricted, and they did not suffer physical violence. However, the work targets set by the company were considered too high, making the work difficult to continue. Santo said the KBRI Phnom Penh provides consular services and protection for Indonesian citizens in accordance with the procedures and service standards applied. This is what allows the KBRI to continue handling the various problems faced by Indonesian citizens in Cambodia, whose numbers have multiplied many times over in recent years, said Santo on Thursday (15/5). Santo explained that the KBRI Phnom Penh immediately carried out verification after receiving the complaint on Wednesday (23/4). After that, the KBRI Phnom Penh issued a passport-equivalent travel document (SPLP) on Saturday (26/4). The Indonesian Ambassador to the Kingdom of Cambodia Santo Darmosumarto has spoken out about the claim of four Indonesian citizens who said they had left an online fraud company. title_en: Health care: the Tuscany system grows. The oncology network is the best in Italy
text_en: Health care: the Tuscany system grows. The oncology network is the best in Italy Florence, 16 May 2025 – Performance is improving for the Tuscan health system, although problems remain in emergency departments and in the overuse of tests and drugs when they are not necessary. This is at least the picture given by 'bersaglio MeS', the annual report prepared by the Management and Health Laboratory of the Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies in Pisa, in collaboration with the Region, Ars Toscana and Ispro. 'According to the study, in 2024, 71% of the roughly 200 indicators monitored improved or remained stable,' said regional health councillor Simone Bezzini, 'the best figure of recent years. On the other hand, 29% signal a critical figure, and on these aspects we must pay the utmost attention so that in 2025 they are overcome.' Among the strengths, the oncology network stands out which, according to the councillor, is 'the best in Italy'. The weak points, on the other hand, concern waiting lists, emergency department times, and also the growth in prescriptions for services and drugs. 'This report is not a report card, but it recognises the merits of Tuscan performance,' said governor Eugenio Giani, 'which in the last year confirms a high percentage of improvement and stability. A tool for developing policy guidelines and policies.' From the data, presented yesterday in Florence, in 2024 there was an increase in outpatient services, in particular follow-up visits, which exceed 2019 levels. Admissions rose to 502,072, 8% below pre-Covid levels, but with a recovery of surgical admissions. In many health companies, days of stay in surgical and medical areas have fallen. For first visits, the share of those booked against those prescribed went from 63% in 2023 to 60% in 2024, while diagnostic tests did better (from 60 to 64%). Abandonments without emergency department cover remained stable at 3.9%. Appropriateness is not going well: musculoskeletal MRIs rose from 21 to 23 per thousand inhabitants and repeat MRIs from 5.4% to 6.1%, while antibiotic consumption in children rose by 10%, and polytherapy with more than 10 drugs reaches almost 8% among over-65s. As explained by Professor Milena Vainieri, head of the Management and Health Laboratory of the Sant'Anna, along the oncology pathway waiting times for priority procedures improved (breast, rectum, uterus, melanoma, thyroid), while for the colon volumes of activity increased, but so did waiting times. Positive data for post-operative follow-up for breast cancer: checks rose from 84% to 86.8%, and tele-visits are beginning to spread. In the maternal and child pathway, vaginal births after caesarean rose (from 25 to 27.5%) and the appropriate use of episiotomy improved (8.4%). In chronic care, hospitalisations for conditions sensitive to outpatient care fell, while emergency department visits rose. Overall, the increase in health spending (+5.06% in the fourth quarter of 2024) is in line with the national average (+5.35%), although the indicators of economic and financial sustainability point to a growing imbalance between costs and revenues. title_en: Load plan sets a physical programme for Al Ahly players during the break before training resumes
text_en: Load plan sets a physical programme for Al Ahly players during the break before training resumes Thank you for reading. News about: Load plan sets a physical programme for Al Ahly players during the break before training resumes. And now the details of the news. CAIRO – Samia Sayed – Al Ahly's coaching staff has set a physical programme for the players during the rest period they have received, to carry out specific training during the holiday the players were granted for two weeks following the crowning as Egyptian Super Cup champions. Andres Andoya set the Al Ahly load plan, a physical programme for the players throughout the rest period: the players will have passive rest with no additional training in the first week of the holiday, and will do gym training and some physical exercises during the second week of the rest period. Al Ahly is on passive rest until 10 January of this month, and will resume training next Thursday at the Mokhtar El Tetsh stadium at the start of preparations for the upcoming competitions. Meanwhile, Al Ahly officials are awaiting the result of the X-ray that the Moroccan player Reda Slim will undergo before the Red team's return to training on 11 January of this month, in order to decide his position regarding group training. Although Reda Slim is currently in the final stage of his rehabilitation from his recent shoulder injury, his return to group training still needs a period of time, and he will not return to group training when the team returns on 11 January of this month. The X-ray that Reda Slim will undergo will determine the date of his return to Al Ahly's group training, as the player is close to finishing the rehabilitation programme he is currently following to recover from the shoulder injury, but the player will need another period of rehabilitation after the X-ray of no less than a week, and he will not take part in group training with the team next Thursday. Reda Slim suffered an injury to the anterior muscle during a rehabilitation programme to recover from collarbone surgery, so he was given several days of rest before starting a rehabilitation programme for the anterior muscle injury and another programme to recover from the collarbone injury. Reda Slim suffered a shoulder injury during the Sundowns match in the African League last November, after which he underwent collarbone surgery. title_en: Suspected long Covid: what do I need to know?
text_en: Suspected long Covid: what do I need to know? Treating the consequences of Corona Suspected long Covid: what do I need to know? Berlin · The infection is over, but symptoms remain: this is relatively rare, but for those affected it entails major limitations. What the signs of long Covid are, and what help is available. Corona infections whose symptoms or effects last longer than those of other infections and affect life and everyday routines: could this be long Covid? When does one actually speak of long Covid, and how can it be treated? The Stiftung Gesundheitswissen gives answers and tips to understand symptoms and find suitable points of contact. What is meant by long Covid? Long Covid refers to persistent health problems that last at least four weeks after a COVID-19 infection. The most common symptoms include extreme tiredness and exhaustion, a feeling of no longer being able to manage everyday things, such as climbing three flights of stairs or making a cup of coffee, the foundation says. The technical term for this is fatigue. In addition there are breathing difficulties, muscle pain, and problems with concentration and memory. The term long Covid is not clearly defined; according to the World Health Organization (WHO) it describes health complaints lasting longer than four weeks after a Corona infection and not explained by another illness. Anyone who finds after a COVID illness that complaints do not go away, come back or appear anew should seek medical advice, the Stiftung Gesundheitswissen says. Whom do I contact if I suspect long Covid? The first step should be the GP practice. An initial assessment of the symptoms can take place there. It can be helpful to keep a symptom diary to show at the doctor's appointment. Through a series of examinations the complaints can be classified and possibly linked to long Covid. Typical symptoms such as exhaustion, shortness of breath and concentration problems are identified with various tests. Depending on the complaints, the GP or family doctor may prescribe various measures such as breathing therapy or physiotherapy, the foundation says. What can I do myself? For self-management of some symptoms, the Stiftung Gesundheitswissen has listed tips and exercises on its website, for example for breathing difficulties and concentration problems: https://www.stiftung-gesundheitswissen.de/wissen/long-covid/leben-mit. There is also a link to self-help groups there. © dpa-infocom, dpa:240816-930-204642/1

title_en: Adonis Georgiadis: "Your strike has not succeeded" - The dialogue with the doctors and nurses outside
text_en: Adonis Georgiadis: "Your strike has not succeeded" - The dialogue with the doctors and nurses outside Adonis Georgiadis held a conversation with the protesting doctors and nurses of the National Health System (ESY) who had gathered outside the Ministry of Health. "Your strike has not succeeded. People need to know that all hospitals are operating today while the nationwide strike of doctors and nurses in public hospitals is under way," the Minister of Health stressed. A woman can be heard telling him, "Mr Georgiadis, you do not represent the thousands of doctors," with the minister replying, "Where did you see the thousands of doctors?" One of the doctors told the minister: "We cannot put our hand in patients' pockets. We want the money we are entitled to as scientists, for the state to be able to give it to us," with the minister replying: "How much do you want?" The dialogue became more heated, with someone else shouting, "according to what the Council of State says". title_en: Sunburn: What you need to watch out for (vid)
text_en: Sunburn: What you need to watch out for (vid) Sunburn can cause immediate pain, redness and discomfort, but the risks extend far beyond these short-term symptoms. Even when the visible signs of sunburn fade, the damage remains, often leading to long-term consequences. Sunburn accelerates skin ageing and is a major cause of basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma, the deadliest form of skin cancer. The good news is that sunburn can be fully prevented, and the best time to start protecting your skin is now. Sunburn is an inflammatory reaction to ultraviolet (UV) damage to the outer layers of the skin. At the centre of this reaction is melanin, a pigment that gives your skin its colour and helps protect it from the sun's rays. Melanin works by darkening your skin when it is exposed to sunlight. The amount of melanin you produce is determined by genetics, which is why some people burn while others tan. Both tanning and burning are signs of cell damage in the skin. For those with less melanin, prolonged sun exposure without protection can cause redness, swelling and pain in skin cells, commonly known as sunburn. Sunburns can range from mild to blistering. After a sunburn, your skin may begin to peel. This peeling is a sign that your body is trying to shed damaged cells. Never try to peel your skin yourself; let it come off naturally. Prevention and treatment of sunburn Prevention 1. Use sunscreen. 2. Seek shade. 3. Avoid sunbeds. Treatment 1. Cold showers. 2. Drink plenty of water to help your skin recover from the dehydration caused by sun exposure. 3. Avoid further sun exposure.

title_en: Details of the Al Ahly stars' contract crisis: financial disputes and sudden decisions
text_en: Details of the Al Ahly stars' contract crisis: financial disputes and sudden decisions We present to our visitors the most important and latest details of the story: Details of the Al Ahly stars' contract crisis: financial disputes and sudden decisions, in the following article. Ahmed Gouda - Cairo - Media personality Medhat Shalaby confirmed that in the past period a number of Al Ahly players have taken steps to request financial amendments to their contracts, in light of the disparity in salaries within the first-team squad. Details of the Al Ahly stars' contract crisis. Shalaby said, while presenting the programme Ya Masaa al-Anwar on MBC Masr 2, that a large group of Al Ahly players have submitted official requests to amend their salaries, and that the management has agreed to some of these demands, most notably for player Imam Ashour. Shalaby added that Mohamed Youssef, Al Ahly's sporting director, refused to accede to Hussein El Shahat's request to amend his contract, explaining that El Shahat currently earns 16 million pounds per season, a salary within the first tier of the team, but his low share of appearances in recent matches was a main reason for refusing to raise his pay. Shalaby noted that the duo Mohamed Magdy 'Afsha' and Marwan Attia are paid the second-tier salary, which amounts to 12 million pounds, and that the management informed them it would study the file of renewing and amending their contracts in the coming period. Shalaby explained that there are other players from the younger age group who earn lower salaries, including Mostafa Shobeir, Mostafa Mokhlouf, Ahmed Nabil 'Koka' and Karim El Dabes, noting that the football administration is also studying a re-evaluation of their contracts according to their rates of participation and technical level.

title_en: Rashad Fettal joins Real Madrid: a promising deal from Morocco
text_en: Rashad Fettal joins Real Madrid: a promising deal from Morocco We present to our visitors the most important and latest details of the story: Rashad Fettal joins Real Madrid: a promising deal from Morocco, in the following article. Ahmed Gouda - Cairo - The Moroccan newspaper Al Muntakhab revealed details of the transfer of young Moroccan forward Rashad Fettal, aged 20, to Spanish club Real Madrid, a step that reflects the continuation of the Merengues' policy of investing in rising talents. Rashad Fettal joins Real Madrid... a promising deal from Morocco According to the newspaper, the Spanish club Almería officially announced on the platform X that it had reached a final agreement with Real Madrid regarding the transfer of the young Moroccan international, wishing him success in his new journey with the royal club. The newspaper explained that Rashad Fettal, who is considered one of the most prominent talents in the Moroccan attacking line, has signed a contract with Real Madrid running until 2028, where he is scheduled to begin his career with the reserve team Real Madrid Castilla, replacing forward Gonzalo García, who recently shone by scoring 4 goals in the Club World Cup currently being held in the United States. According to the Spanish newspaper Marca, the total value of the deal is 6 million euros, of which 900 thousand euros is a fixed amount that Real Madrid will pay to Almería, with additional clauses linked to the player's performance that could raise the value to 1.5 million euros, depending on his number of appearances and the goals he scores in the Castilla shirt. The Fettal deal reinforces Real Madrid's move towards building a new generation of talent, and confirms the growing presence of Moroccan stars at the biggest European clubs.

title_en: Eurovision Song Contest (ESC) in Vienna: candidate from Sweden collapses before final

Before the big final, nerves are likely to be frayed for some of the acts. The Swedish candidate Felicia Eriksson (24) also seems to have been under enormous pressure: during the last preparations she suddenly collapsed. As Lotta Furebäck, head of the Swedish delegation, explained to the press on site, the 24-year-old collapsed on Friday evening during the dress rehearsal for the final, reports the Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet. According to her, lack of fluids, great heat and the artist's tight-fitting clothing caused her fainting spell. Felicia already felt unwell in the green room and was somewhat dizzy. When we arrived downstairs in the box, she collapsed, Furebäck said. A doctor was called immediately. According to the delegation head, the Swedish artist, who is taking part with the song My System, received medical care on site. Afterwards she was taken to the hotel to rest. If she now drinks enough, eats something and rests, I believe she will be fully fit again tomorrow, Furebäck said confidently. The doctors had also expressed no concerns about Felicia's final performance. Under the circumstances, Felicia feels completely fine again. The delegation head further explained that Felicia's collapse is by no means related to her voice problems earlier in the week. According to the Swedish broadcaster SVT, the EDM artist had complained of a voice that was barely recognisable.

title_en: Urgent warning about the beautiful Mediterranean island that has become a dump full of rats
text_en: Urgent warning about the beautiful Mediterranean island that has become a dump full of rats Comino, the small island of the Maltese archipelago that is considered one of the most beautiful in the Mediterranean Sea, has become a dump full of rats due to excess tourism. Although Malta's tourism authorities describe Comino as 'the most beautiful place in the Mediterranean', activists say the uncontrolled influx of visitors is destroying the island. As reported by the Hungarian media outlet Travelo, although Comino's surface area is only 3.5 square kilometres, up to 10,000 tourists land on the island each day during the summer months. This produces enormous amounts of rubbish. 'The island is full of bars where parties are organised, with loud music, alcoholic drinks and snacks that customers then abandon as rubbish, which is the perfect food source for the growing rat population on Comino,' the outlet highlights. Andre Callus, a member of the activist group Moviment Graffitti, demands radical changes from the country's authorities in the management of this Mediterranean island, as the situation is 'unbearable'. 'It is a nightmare for the residents of Gozo and Malta, and that is why they no longer go there. Comino has been taken over by intense commercial interests. It is a very small place, but 11 kiosks sell food and drink. They want to squeeze every last bit of profit out of the island,' Callus stressed in statements to The Daily Telegraph. The Government of Malta is trying to strike the difficult balance between protecting the island of Comino and promoting tourism, which accounts for 15% of the country's GDP. In this sense, Malta's Minister of Tourism, Ian Borg, has proposed reducing the number of daily visitors to Comino from 10,000 to 5,000, reviewing the number of licensed bars and increasing the installation of public toilets. title_en: New electricity auctions launched in Ukraine: what this changes for business and the public
text_en: New electricity auctions launched in Ukraine: what this changes for business and the public Will the new mechanism help hold back prices? The first long-term electricity sales auctions have taken place in Ukraine. The government expects them to make prices for business predictable and, in the longer term, to help attract investment in new power plants. Whether the new mechanism can change the situation was assessed in comments to RBC-Ukraine by energy experts Gennadiy Ryabtsev and Volodymyr Omelchenko. Key points: on 13 July the first long-term electricity sales auctions took place in Ukraine. Business can buy electricity under contracts for a quarter, half a year and a year. Experts believe the new mechanism will help enterprises better plan their costs, but will not be a revolution for the market. Bank lending for new power plants continues to be held back by military risks. No noticeable impact on prices for the public or on the number of power outages is expected in the near future. How the first trades went: results, prices and scandals The launch of the auctions became possible after changes by the Cabinet of Ministers to resolution No. 499. The first trades took place on 13–14 July for the supply of electricity in August–September. Energoatom and Ukrhydroenergo sold the resource in lots of 5 MW. Companies sold the entire volume, 92 232 MWh, on the first day alone. Prices fluctuated within 5005–5145 UAH/MWh. Most lots were bought by traders, and among final consumers only Ukrzaliznytsia and MHP won. The trades immediately sparked a scandal. People's Deputy Andriy Herus, head of the Verkhovna Rada committee on energy and housing and utilities, suspected manipulation because of a 39% collapse in demand and prices on the adjacent day-ahead market. He stated that enlarging the lots allowed part of the resource to be sold more cheaply, as a result of which the state company lost about 50 million UAH. At the same time, according to some estimates, the average price of about 5 000 UAH is entirely market-based and shows no signs of artificial reduction, and the participation of industrial leaders is a positive signal. Will it be easier for business to plan its costs? As explained by Gennadiy Ryabtsev, Doctor of Science in public administration and director of special projects at the Psykheya R&D centre, electricity is a basic resource for most enterprises, so a predictable price even a few months ahead makes it easier to plan production costs. At the same time, the expert stresses that the effect of the new auctions should not be overstated. In his words, at present we are talking about only 2–4% of electricity that Energoatom and Ukrhydroenergo will sell. Therefore only some enterprises will be able to use such contracts. Volodymyr Omelchenko, director of energy programmes at the Razumkov Centre, shares this view. He calls the very idea of long-term contracts correct, since this is how most European energy markets work. However, Ukrainian companies are still wary of fixing a price for a long period because of high market volatility. Will banks lend more to new power plants? One of the main arguments in favour of long-term contracts is that they should make investment in energy more predictable. However, according to Gennadiy Ryabtsev, today the main obstacle for banks is not electricity prices. 'Banks are afraid to lend to energy projects because of military risks. If a facility can be destroyed in the next strike, no long-term contract will compensate for that,' the expert explains. Omelchenko also does not expect the launch of the auctions to automatically trigger an investment boom. This is a positive signal for the market, but without a comprehensive reform of the energy sector it will not be a decisive factor for investors. Why were the lots limited to 5 MW? text_en:
Woman, 29, asks police to speed up case! Raped and robbed by a lecherous guy who pretended to be a good citizen helping after her motorbike fell

Today (16 March), in front of the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) headquarters, Mr Thamanan Taengthim, or "Sergeant Kings Saphan Mai", brought Ms B (pseudonym), aged 29, to meet investigators of the Crime Suppression Division to seek justice, after she was lured by criminals who pretended to help when her motorbike fell, and then raped and robbed.

Meanwhile two men on a grey Filano motorbike with red plates and a Scoopy came in pretending to help. She recognised the owner of the Filano very clearly. But after helping to lift the bike up, she lost consciousness and knew nothing more, even though her head had not hit the ground, so she suspects she may have been drugged after the man who came close to her.

Ms B went on to say that when she woke again at around 10.00–11.00, she found herself in a room in the Lam Luk Ka 27 alley area, naked, and found the man who had helped her lying in that room, whose face and vehicle she clearly remembered. She felt she had been raped without her consent. She also found that over a thousand baht in cash was missing. title_en: How do Vietnamese enterprises 'raise capital' at the Ho Chi Minh City International Financial Centre?
text_en: How do Vietnamese enterprises 'raise capital' at the Ho Chi Minh City International Financial Centre? According to Dr Cấn Văn Lực, the Ho Chi Minh City International Financial Centre (IFC HCMC) is expected not only to become a driver of institutional reform, approaching international practice, but is also regarded as one of the most important channels for attracting and connecting international capital flows and supplementing resources for socio-economic development, as Vietnam needs 260–280 billion USD for development up to 2030. How can capital be accessed through the IFC? Sharing about the opportunities for enterprises to access capital at IFC HCMC, at an event held on 16 May in HCMC, Associate Professor Dr Nguyễn Hữu Huân, Vice Chairman of the IFC HCMC governing body, said that although it has been operating for less than half a year, many important components of the centre have already been promoted, with the aim of quickly forming an international-standard financial ecosystem. One of the IFC's biggest goals is to develop the capital market and attract capital flows for domestic and regional enterprises, in order to ease pressure on the banking system. In the context of Vietnam's target of double-digit growth, the economy's capital needs are estimated at up to 70–80 billion USD per year, apart from the traditional credit channel. At present there are several channels for enterprises to access capital through IFC HCMC. The first is the capital market channel. The IFC also plans to build an international stock exchange with technology support and cooperation from Nasdaq and the London Stock Exchange. According to the orientation, this exchange will serve not only Vietnamese enterprises but also FDI enterprises and enterprises in the region. In the future, investors in HCMC may trade international shares through cross-listing and dual-listing mechanisms. The second is bond issuance, especially international green bonds, with many regulations creating a favourable legal basis to attract capital flows, especially green capital for enterprises undergoing green transformation. Alongside large enterprises with the opportunity to access capital through IFC, small enterprises and startups also have many opportunities to mobilise capital through IFC via the community capital exchange. At this community capital exchange, small and start-up enterprises can raise up to 700,000 USD per year, a channel that helps small enterprises obtain additional capital for their production and business in the coming period. title_en: Basilicata on fire: vast blaze at Montalbano Jonico near the town centre
text_en: Basilicata on fire: vast blaze at Montalbano Jonico near the town centre Basilicata is going through difficult hours because of the scorching heatwave and the fires breaking out in several areas of the region. Among them, one of the most worrying blazes broke out in the last few hours in the Montalbano Jonico area, in the province of Matera, seriously threatening the safety of the local population. The flames have attacked a vast area bordering the town centre, involving in particular the outskirts of via Sant'Antuono, near the public gardens of the town in the province of Matera, via Caracciolo in the heart of the town, and part of the picturesque Calanchi Reserve. The situation is made even more critical by the speed with which the fire is spreading, fuelled by winds and scorching temperatures approaching 40°. The toll of the damage is already significant: several hectares of land have been destroyed, a car has been completely burnt out and dense black smoke is making the air unbreathable in the town centre. This situation is putting great strain on residents, who are forced to live with the acrid smell of smoke and the fear that the flames may come even closer to their homes. Numerous teams from the local Fire Brigade companies are currently engaged in tackling the emergency, assisted by many volunteers from Civil Protection. The intervention of a Canadair water bomber has also been requested.

title_en: Russia: Ukrainian attack targets 'Voronezh trains'
text_en: Russia: Ukrainian attack targets 'Voronezh trains' The Russian Voronezh region was attacked today (Sunday) by a drone, which targeted the main railway station, injuring a railway worker and damaging an electricity line. Governor Alexander Joseph wrote on Telegram: 'According to preliminary information, a technician at a railway station in one of the municipalities was injured and taken to hospital.' The Russian official added that the attack by Ukrainian forces on the region caused train journeys to be disrupted. The Russian Ministry of Defence, which announces only the number of drones destroyed by air defence units and not the number that Ukraine launches, said on Telegram that nine drones had been shot down over the Voronezh region in south-west Russia. The ministry said its defence systems had destroyed a total of 46 Ukrainian drones during the night, all of them in areas west of Moscow. However, Reuters has not been able to independently verify the Russian reports. Ukraine has not issued any comment so far.
